blocks.text: The opening of this episode contrasts imperial ambition with moral refuge. Aurangzeb hardens his rule into forced Islamization, while Guru Tegh Bahadur emerges as the defender to whom the distressed and threatened turn for protection.

The page gathers the pressure of the age by describing how coercion expands and how Hindu communities feel the tightening force of Mughal authority. In that atmosphere, Guru Tegh Bahadur's presence becomes not merely respected but necessary.

Read with the following page, this fragment is the doorway into a larger martyrdom narrative. It establishes Aurangzeb's tyranny as the condition that will make spiritual courage, consultation, and sacrifice central to what follows.
